content.text: The chapters depict working-class poverty, exploitation, drunkenness, and hypocrisy in Mugsborough. At the *Cricketers*, workers drink and gamble; Easton returns home drunk to Ruth, while a semi-drunk man is violently expelled into the road. Owen explains the “Great Money Trick”: workers produce society’s wealth but receive insufficient wages, while capitalists appropriate the surplus. He divides society into useless elites, exploiters, unnecessary workers, and productive workers. Unemployment then devastates families: the Lindens lose their home and enter the workhouse; Newman is imprisoned for unpaid rates; children go hungry. Charitable schemes merely humiliate the poor. Meanwhile, council “Brigands” plan to sell failing electric works to the town. At home, Slyme makes unwanted advances toward Ruth. Owen, ill and despairing, contemplates death for himself and his family.
